messages:
maria: heads-up — i'm prototyping a new grafana page to correlate tenant burst patterns with network egress, pcie saturation, and thermal/fan behavior. goal: find why some bursts cause evictions in us-west-2
kevin: sounds useful. is this tied to the eviction spike yesterday during the batch job ramp?
maria: yep. timeline: tenant A spiked token throughput -> node net tx peaked -> pci_e2e backlog rose -> gpu temp climbed -> one eviction. curious if network stalls are causing long vram stalls that look like memory pressure to the scheduler.
sylvia: metrics we should include: rate(tokens_generated[1m]) by (tenant), node_network_transmit_bytes_total, nvidia_pci_tx_queued, nvlink_retry_count, nvidia_gpu_temp_celsius, nvidia_fan_speed_rpm, scheduler_eviction_total{reason=~".*memory.*|.*stall.*"}
maria: here's a promql prototype for tenant vs egress heatmap (start point):
```
# per-tenant token rate per minute (label tenant must exist on ingestion)
sum by (tenant, region) (rate(app_tokens_generated_total[1m]))

# node-level network TX (bytes/sec)
sum by (instance, region) (rate(node_network_transmit_bytes_total[1m]))
```
jon: cardinality is a concern if we label tokens by tenant for all events. we should record-rule aggregate to tenant:region hourly or have a metrics-shaper job to emit top-20 tenants per cluster as a derived metric. otherwise grafana will explode.
sylvia: agree. also recommend using topk(25, ...) in the heatmap and a fallback recording rule that keeps per-tenant series but only for last 48h. older data can be downsampled.
lee: panel layout idea:
- main: time heatmap (tenants on y) showing token-rate bursts (hover shows tenant id + estimated egress)
- overlay line: cluster net tx 95p (region-level)
- small stacked bars: eviction events per-node (color by reason)
- right column: sparkline panel for avg gpu_temp and fan_rpm for nodes involved in the burst
- bottom: table join to billing estimate (egress bytes * $/GB) per tenant for selected time range
kevin: can we annotate the times when pci queue length > threshold so we see correlation? also tie in "pci_link_utilization" if available.
maria: good call. i've got a crude pci queue metric from the driver exporter: nvidia_pci_tx_queue_length. sample promql: `sum by (instance) (avg_over_time(nvidia_pci_tx_queue_length[5m]))` then annotate when > 200
jon: alerting suggestion: composite rule that fires when region_net_tx_p95 > 0.9 * iface_capacity AND node_gpu_temp_95p > 80C AND eviction_rate > 0 for same 5m window. maybe "Potential burst-induced eviction" severity=warning. keep it noisy-proof with 3min for firing.
sylvia: also include a low-cardinality proxy metric for fan ramp rate: `increase(nvidia_fan_speed_rpm[2m])` > X. That helps detect reactive cooling rather than pure thermal drift.
kevin: cost side — we should overlay estimated egress cost per tenant as lee mentioned. billing team can provide a mapping job to attach `tenant` labels to net bytes per flow; otherwise approximate by mapping top talkers via ip->tenant.
maria: action items:
- maria: build dashboard skeleton (heatmap + overlay + eviction bars) and push dashboard json to grafana/dashboards/review by EOD Fri
- jon: sketch recording rules for per-tenant aggregates and drop-high-cardinality pipeline by Thu
- sylvia: give a pref for topk threshold + fan ramp thresholds; i'll include in the alert rule
- kevin: coordinate with billing on a one-off ip->tenant mapping job for the PoC
- lee: i'll add layout mockups to the ticket and include suggested panel sizes
ops-bot: deployment scheduled: grafana-dashboard/maria/tenant-lattice-v1 will be created in staging at 1728398000
maria: scheduling a 30m sync Thu 10:30 PT to review the first pass. ping me if you want edit access to the dashboard json. :thumbsup:
